resources.string: A keyboard that keeps your typing on your phone
This app has no internet permission. It cannot send anything anywhere, because it has no way to. Everything it does happens on this device.
In password, email, phone and payment fields the keyboard turns off suggestions, learning and history entirely.
Your personal dictionary, the learn-as-you-type switch, and a status screen that says why suggestions are or are not appearing.
If suggestions are not appearing, this says why.

Off by default. When you turn this on, the keyboard counts which words you tend to put next to each other and uses that to order its suggestions. The counts stay on this phone, encrypted, and there is nowhere for them to go — this app has no internet permission.

It never stores what you wrote — only how often one word followed another, as numbers. It never learns in password, payment, email, phone, name or address fields. A pair you have typed only once is never suggested back to you.

This deletes everything the keyboard has learned about how you write, and the key that unlocks it, so the stored bytes can never be read again. Your personal dictionary is separate and is not touched.
Words you add here are stored encrypted on this device and never leave it. The keyboard adds nothing on its own — only what you type in below. It never stores sentences or a record of what you type.
This deletes every word you have added and destroys the encryption key, so the stored data can never be read again — including by this app. It cannot be undone.
